blueprint_topic: Management of Care — infection-prevention program leadership and systems coordination
stem: A hospital is reviewing the responsibilities of the team member who manages its infection prevention and control (IPC) program. Which activity set best reflects that role?

options.A: Coordinate ongoing HAI and transmission surveillance, monitor IPC adherence and feedback, maintain evidence-based policies, and support personnel education.
options.B: Lead outbreak investigations while routine surveillance, policy updates, and IPC education are managed separately by unit leaders between outbreaks.
options.C: Maintain HAI surveillance and reporting while leaving adherence monitoring, feedback, and staff competency activities outside the IPC program.
options.D: Focus the program on healthcare-personnel exposure and illness management while unit quality teams manage patient-care transmission risks and HAI surveillance.

rationale: A is correct. CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices call for one or more qualified individuals trained in IPC to manage the facility's infection-prevention program. The same core framework includes job-specific IPC education, current evidence-based written policies and procedures, monitoring adherence to IPC practices, prompt regular feedback, monitoring infection incidence, and using surveillance to detect transmission. B is incorrect because IPC program functions are ongoing and are not confined to outbreak investigations. C is incorrect because performance monitoring, feedback, and competency-related education are part of the core IPC framework rather than functions outside the program. D is incorrect because occupational exposure and illness management does not replace the program's patient-care infection risks, HAI surveillance, and transmission-prevention responsibilities.
educational_objective: Recognize IPC program management as an ongoing systems role that coordinates surveillance, evidence-based policies, personnel education, adherence monitoring, and feedback to prevent healthcare-associated transmission.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: CDC's Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings; Guideline for Isolation Precautions — Fundamental Elements Needed to Prevent Transmission of Infectious Agents in Healthcare Settings
source_version_date: CDC Core Practices page dated April 12, 2024 and listed in the current CDC Infection Control Guidance Library; Isolation Precautions Fundamental Elements page dated January 31, 2025; accessed 2026-08-20
source_locator: CDC Core Practices Table — Leadership Support: assign one or more qualified individuals with IPC training to manage the facility infection-prevention program and empower their authority. Education and Training: provide job-specific IPC education and current evidence-based written policies/procedures. Performance Monitoring and Feedback: monitor adherence to IPC requirements, provide prompt regular feedback, monitor infection incidence, and use surveillance to detect transmission. Isolation Precautions — II.B Surveillance for HAIs: surveillance is an ongoing systematic activity used to identify infections/transmission and evaluate prevention efforts.
source_claim_supported: Facility IPC program management is an ongoing systems function incorporating qualified leadership, surveillance, evidence-based policy support, education, adherence monitoring, and feedback rather than an outbreak-only or occupational-health-only role.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care, printed page 7/PDF page 11: 'Identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members when providing client care'; 'Participate in performance improvement projects and quality improvement processes'; 'Utilize resources to promote quality client care.'
pdf_visual_verification: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan printed page 7/PDF page 11 visually verified by screenshot on 2026-08-20; no CACHE MISS.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'infection prevention program surveillance adherence feedback education policies HAI' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Retained the IPC-program-management construct and key A while removing only/exclusively cueing. Distractors now represent plausible organizational fragmentation errors involving outbreak response, surveillance-only roles, and occupational-health substitution.

option_audit.A: Correct; summarizes core program functions directly supported by CDC without requiring the IPC manager to personally perform every task.
option_audit.B: Plausible outbreak-response misconception; incorrect because core IPC functions continue outside outbreaks.
option_audit.C: Plausible surveillance-only misconception; incorrect because adherence monitoring, feedback, and education are also core IPC practices.
option_audit.D: Plausible occupational-health overlap misconception; incorrect because patient-care transmission risk and HAI surveillance remain core IPC program functions.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/exclusively/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All options contain comparable operational detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four options are parallel descriptions of program-management scope.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified; B, C, and D each omit or displace CDC-defined core IPC program functions.
